## What it catches

A Debugger value written under the Image File Execution Options key of one of the accessibility programs that the logon screen can start. Windows then runs the debugger instead of the program, as SYSTEM and before anyone has logged on, which gives a shell from the lock screen. Replacing the program's file on disk has the same effect and is not seen here.

```yaml
selection:
  TargetObject|endswith:
  - \Image File Execution Options\sethc.exe\Debugger
  - \Image File Execution Options\utilman.exe\Debugger
  - \Image File Execution Options\osk.exe\Debugger
  - \Image File Execution Options\magnify.exe\Debugger
  - \Image File Execution Options\narrator.exe\Debugger
  - \Image File Execution Options\displayswitch.exe\Debugger
  - \Image File Execution Options\atbroker.exe\Debugger
condition: selection
```

## Tested on

- fires: `debugger set for sethc.exe`
- fires: `debugger set for utilman.exe`
- fires: `debugger set for osk.exe`
- fires: `debugger set for magnify.exe`
- fires: `debugger set for narrator.exe`
- fires: `debugger set for displayswitch.exe by PowerShell`
- fires: `debugger set for atbroker.exe pointing at a dropped file`
- quiet: `a developer's just-in-time debugger for their own program`
- quiet: `exploit mitigation options set for the sticky keys program`
- quiet: `a debugger set for notepad during troubleshooting`
- quiet: `an assistive technology registered by its installer`

## False positives

- None expected: no ordinary software sets a debugger for these programs

## What it does not see

- The accessibility program's file replaced or renamed on disk, which writes no registry value
- A registry write made offline, from another operating system or a recovery environment
- Registry events not collected for the Image File Execution Options key

## First checks

- Read the debugger path written and who wrote it
- Check the logon screen of the host: Remote Desktop connections that did not complete a logon
- Remove the value and look for the same write on other hosts
